facts.fact: The Salesforce org is the unit of tenancy: each customer has a production org, sandboxes, scratch orgs and Developer Edition orgs are separate orgs with their own users, metadata and API allocations, and there is no account, project or workspace layer above the org for API access (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=platform.create_test_instance.htm&type=5).

A Salesforce org is the tenancy unit of the Salesforce platform, with no higher account or workspace layer for API access (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=platform.create_test_instance.htm&type=5).

Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes can be refreshed every 1 day, Partial Copy every 5 days and Full every 29 days (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=platform.create_test_instance.htm&type=5).

Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes copy metadata only, Partial Copy copies a template-defined sample of data, and Full copies all data and metadata (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000387743&language=en_US&type=1).

Sandbox data storage is 200 MB for Developer (400 MB with a storage upgrade), 1 GB for Developer Pro (2 GB upgraded), 5 GB for Partial Copy, and Full matches production (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=sf.data_sandbox_environments.htm&type=5).
Partial Copy and Full sandboxes are not available in Salesforce Professional Edition (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=sf.data_sandbox_environments.htm&type=5).

Scratch orgs come from a Dev Hub, which can be enabled in Developer, Enterprise, Unlimited or Performance Edition orgs (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_dev.pdf).

Supported scratch org editions are Developer, Enterprise, Group and Professional, and each scratch org has 500 MB of data and 50 MB of file storage (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/sfdx-dev/guide/sfdx-dev-scratch-orgs-editions-and-allocations.html).

Scratch org allocations (active/daily) by Dev Hub edition per DX Developer Guide v68.0 (updated 2026-09-25) are Developer Edition or trial 3/6, Enterprise 40/80, Unlimited 100/200 and Performance 100/200; the daily count is a rolling 24-hour window and partner business orgs differ (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_dev.pdf).

Scratch org duration is 1 to 30 days, set at creation with `sf org create scratch --duration-days`, with a default of 7 days (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_org_create_scratch.html).

`sf org create scratch --duration-days` creates a scratch org and sets its lifetime of 1 to 30 days (default 7) (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_org_create_scratch.html).

The `Einstein1AIPlatform` scratch org feature gives access to Agentforce, Prompt Builder, Model Builder and the Models API (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_dev.pdf).

Using `Einstein1AIPlatform` also requires `einsteinGptSettings > enableEinsteinGptPlatform` in the scratch org definition file's settings (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_dev.pdf).

The `CustomerDataPlatform` and `CustomerDataPlatformLite` scratch org features enable the Data Cloud license in scratch orgs (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_dev.pdf).

Since March 2025 the free Salesforce Developer Edition includes Agentforce and Data Cloud (now Data 360) (https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2025/03/introducing-the-new-salesforce-developer-edition-now-with-agentforce-and-data-cloud).

An April 2026 update added Agentforce Vibes IDE, Claude Sonnet 4.5 as the default coding model and hosted MCP servers to Developer Edition, rolling out to existing orgs gradually (https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2026/04/new-developer-edition-agentforce-vibes-claude-mcp).

Claude Sonnet 4.5 is the default coding model for Agentforce Vibes in Developer Edition after the April 2026 update (https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2026/04/new-developer-edition-agentforce-vibes-claude-mcp).
Data Cloud is now named Data 360 (https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2025/03/introducing-the-new-salesforce-developer-edition-now-with-agentforce-and-data-cloud).

A Developer Edition org can expire if nobody logs in, trial orgs expire on their expiration date, and when a Dev Hub trial or DE org expires its package versions are lost (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_dev.pdf).

One dated Japanese-language Salesforce blog lists 5 MB of data, two Salesforce user licenses and 150 LLM calls per hour for Developer Edition, for non-commercial use (unverified) (https://developer.salesforce.com/jpblogs/2016/04/developer-edition-signup/).

On 2026-09-03 Salesforce launched Core ($195/user/month), Advanced ($395) and Max ($550) editions for Agentforce Sales, Agentforce Service and Agentforce Industries (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/salesforce-simplifies-editions-2026/).

Every 2026 edition (Core, Advanced, Max) bundles Agentforce, Slack and Slackbot, embedded agentic analytics, data security and Premier Success Plans; Advanced is $395/user/month (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/salesforce-simplifies-editions-2026/).

Max Edition ($550/user/month) is one of the three Salesforce editions launched on 2026-09-03 alongside Core and Advanced (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/salesforce-simplifies-editions-2026/).
Pricing on existing legacy editions Enterprise and Unlimited is unchanged by the 2026-09-03 editions change (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/salesforce-simplifies-editions-2026/).
Unlimited Edition is a legacy edition whose pricing is unchanged after the 2026-09-03 launch of Core, Advanced and Max (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/salesforce-simplifies-editions-2026/).

facts.fact: Agentforce 1 Edition became Max Edition, which keeps the Agentforce 1 price of $550/user/month, and the pricing page now shows the card as Max Edition (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/salesforce-simplifies-editions-2026/ ; https://pricingsaas.com/companies/salesforce.agentforce/diffs/2026W41 (secondary)).
Max Edition is $550/user/month and existing Agentforce 1 Edition customers can upgrade to Max at no extra cost (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/salesforce-simplifies-editions-2026/).

Third-party write-ups say the new editions replace Enterprise and Unlimited for new sales, but Salesforce's own announcement only compares against legacy Enterprise and Unlimited and does not state a retirement (secondary) (https://salesforcedictionary.com/blogs/salesforce-core-advanced-max-editions-2026).

Retirement of Unlimited Edition for new sales is claimed only by third-party sources such as SalesforceBen; Salesforce does not state a retirement (secondary) (https://www.salesforceben.com/salesforce-announces-3-replacement-editions-bundling-ai-slack-and-security/).

Enterprises buy Salesforce licenses, add-ons and extra API calls through a Salesforce account executive or in-org through the Your Account app (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.pdf).
Flex Credits can be bought as Pre-Purchase, PayGo or Pre-Commit, with Pre-Commit described as widely available later this year (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/pricing/).

Day-one asks for an engineer on a client engagement: a named user in a Developer Pro or Partial Copy sandbox plus a Dev Hub-enabled org if using scratch orgs, the org's My Domain login URL, an external client app plus a dedicated Salesforce Integration user, confirmation that Agentforce, Einstein generative AI and Data 360 are provisioned and which licenses exist (Einstein Agent licenses, Agentforce add-ons, Flex Credits), whether API Access Control is on, and the MFA/SSO setup (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_dev.pdf).

The org's My Domain login URL takes the form `https://<domain>.my.salesforce.com`, or `<domain>--<sandbox>.sandbox.my.salesforce.com` for sandboxes (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_dev.pdf).
An integration needs an external client app plus a dedicated Salesforce Integration user (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=platform.integration_user.htm&type=5).

External client apps (ECAs) replace connected apps: creating connected apps is restricted as of Spring '26, existing connected apps keep working, and Salesforce recommends ECAs (REST API Developer Guide v68.0, updated 2026-10-09) (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_rest.pdf).
As of Spring '26 anyone who must create new connected apps has to contact Salesforce Support (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/api-rest/guide/intro-oauth-and-connected-apps.html).

Orgs authorized for Salesforce CLI need an ECA (preferred) or a connected app, and the default `Salesforce CLI` connected app is supplied (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_dev.pdf).

If you authorize a Dev Hub and plan to run `sf org create scratch|sandbox`, you must create a connected app instead of an ECA (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_dev.pdf).

`ExtlClntAppGlobalOauthSettings` is a Metadata API type (API 60.0+) holding the OAuth flow switches of an external client app (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_meta.pdf).

In `ExtlClntAppGlobalOauthSettings`, `isClientCredentialsFlowEnabled` turns on client credentials, `certificate` (a PEM certificate) enables the JWT Bearer flow, `isDeviceFlowEnabled` turns on the device flow, `isTokenExchangeEnabled` and `isSecretRequiredForTokenExchange` cover token exchange, and `isRefreshTokenRotationEnabled` turns on refresh token rotation (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_meta.pdf).

`isPkceRequired` defaults to true, `isNamedUserJwtEnabled` (API 61.0+) issues JWT-based access tokens instead of opaque ones, and `isCodeCredFlowEnabled` (API 61.0+) turns on the Authorization Code and Credentials flow for headless login (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_meta.pdf).
An ECA enables the JWT Bearer flow when a PEM `certificate` is set in `ExtlClntAppGlobalOauthSettings` (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_meta.pdf).

In `ExtlClntAppOauthConfigurablePolicies`, `clientCredentialsFlowUser` names the execution user that client credentials tokens are issued for, and this user must have the API Only permission (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_meta.pdf).

The client credentials flow returns no refresh token, scopes are assigned on the app rather than in the request, and anyone holding the consumer key and secret can mint tokens (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.meta_configure_client_credentials_flow_for_external_client_apps.htm&language=en_US&type=5).

`sf org login jwt --client-id <consumer key> --jwt-key-file server.key --username <user> --instance-url <My Domain URL>` authorizes an org with a private key whose `server.crt` certificate is uploaded to the ECA (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_dev.pdf).
Salesforce points to the JWT Bearer flow for CI and server-to-server integrations that need a user context (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000886201&language=en_US&type=1).

facts.fact: Salesforce publishes a guide to migrating from the OAuth username-password flow to client credentials, as the username-password flow is on the way out (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=000886201&language=en_US&type=1).
SOAP API `login()` in API versions 31.0-64.0 retires in Summer '27 (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005387171&language=en_US&type=1).

The org setting `OauthOidcSettings.blockOAuthUnPwFlow` blocks the OAuth username-password flow and `blockOAuthUsrAgtFlow` blocks the user-agent flow (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_meta.pdf).

facts.target: Minimum Access - API Only Integrations profile
facts.fact: The Salesforce Integration user license grants API-only access and is paired with the `Minimum Access - API Only Integrations` profile, from which API-only access can't be removed (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=platform.integration_user.htm&type=5).

facts.target: Salesforce API Integration permission set license
facts.fact: Extra rights for Salesforce Integration users come through permission sets that use the `Salesforce API Integration` permission set license (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=platform.integration_user.htm&type=5).

The Salesforce Integration user license was introduced in Winter '23 (release 242) (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_api_integration_license.htm&language=en_US&release=242).

Enterprise, Unlimited and Performance Edition orgs get five Salesforce Integration user licenses at no cost, Developer Edition orgs get one, and more can be purchased (https://admin.salesforce.com/blog/2023/best-practices-for-configuring-your-integration-user).

facts.source: Minimum Access - API Only Integrations profile
facts.target: Salesforce API Only System Integrations profile
facts.fact: `Minimum Access - API Only Integrations` replaced `Salesforce API Only System Integrations` in Summer '23 (release 248) because the old profile wrongly granted CRUD on custom objects (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_api_new_user_profile.htm&language=en_US&release=248&type=5).

Recommended setup for an external agent calling Salesforce REST APIs: create a Salesforce Integration user with the `Minimum Access - API Only Integrations` profile, grant object and field access through permission sets on the `Salesforce API Integration` PSL, create an ECA with client credentials (or JWT bearer) and set that user as the execution user, pre-authorize the app by profile or permission set, and call the token endpoint (https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2024/02/invoke-rest-apis-with-the-salesforce-integration-user-and-oauth-client-credentials).

The OAuth token endpoint is `https://<MyDomain>.my.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` (https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2024/02/invoke-rest-apis-with-the-salesforce-integration-user-and-oauth-client-credentials).

The Salesforce Integration user is set as the execution user of an ECA using client credentials (or JWT bearer) for an external agent (https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2024/02/invoke-rest-apis-with-the-salesforce-integration-user-and-oauth-client-credentials).

Agent API OAuth setup needs an ECA with scopes `api`, `refresh_token`/`offline_access`, `chatbot_api` and `sfap_api`, the client credentials flow and Issue JWT-based access tokens for named users enabled, require secret for the web server and refresh token flows and require PKCE turned off, and a Run As user with at least API Only access (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/agent-api-get-started.html).

The Agent API token is minted against the My Domain URL, and any flow that yields a JWT-based access token works (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/agent-api-get-started.html).

On Agent API session creation, `bypassUser: true` runs the session as the agent's assigned agent user and `false` runs it as the token's user (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/agent-api-get-started.html).

Agentforce Service Agents run as a dedicated agent user with the `Einstein Agent` user license and the `Einstein Agent User` profile, not a seat-consuming Salesforce license; that user has no password and can't log in interactively (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=ai.agent_user.htm&type=5).
An Agentforce agent user is assigned the `Einstein Agent User` profile (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=ai.agent_user.htm&type=5).
`sf org create agent-user` creates an Agentforce agent user (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_org_create_agent-user.html).

Employee agents (formerly Agentforce (Default) / Copilot) run in the signed-in employee's context, and access to a specific employee agent is controlled with permission sets or profiles (Manage Employee Agent Access) (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_manage_aea_access.htm&language=en_US&type=5).

`OauthOidcSettings` has a boolean `agentAuthLinking` field with no description in the Metadata API guide; it may relate to linking agent and user identities (unverified) (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_meta.pdf).

facts.fact: Salesforce recommends the enhanced My Domain login URL ending in `my.salesforce.com` (for example `https://exciting.sandbox.my.salesforce.com`), not the `.lightning.force.com` URL, because it survives instance migrations; set it in `sfdcLoginUrl` or pass `--instance-url` (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_dev.pdf).
MFA has been contractually required since 2022-02-01 for both direct and SSO logins (https://security.salesforce.com/mfa/).

Salesforce enforces MFA for all users beginning 2026-06-26, after which the Require multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all direct UI logins setting can't be turned off (https://admin.salesforce.com/blog/2026/prepare-your-org-for-salesforce-mfa-enforcement).

SSO logins satisfy the MFA requirement only if the IdP sends valid AMR/ACR claims, otherwise users are prompted to enroll in Salesforce MFA (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005321563&language=en_US&type=1).

Admins and users with powerful permissions such as `Modify All Data` must present a phishing-resistant MFA signal or enroll in Salesforce phishing-resistant MFA (https://admin.salesforce.com/blog/2026/prepare-your-org-for-salesforce-mfa-enforcement).
Supported Salesforce MFA methods are Salesforce Authenticator, third-party TOTP apps, WebAuthn/U2F security keys and built-in authenticators (https://security.salesforce.com/mfa/).

Salesforce supports SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect SSO through My Domain and Auth. Providers; the current doc pages could not be verified (unverified) (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=sf.security_overview_2fa.htm&type=5).
Salesforce supports OpenID Connect SSO through Auth. Providers (unverified) (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=sf.security_overview_2fa.htm&type=5).
The Salesforce Identity documentation covers SCIM user provisioning (unverified) (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=sf.security_overview_2fa.htm&type=5).

Salesforce documents no keyless OIDC workload identity federation from GitHub Actions or other clouds; CI pipelines use the JWT bearer flow with a stored private key (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/sfdx_dev.pdf).

Salesforce access is additive: each user has exactly one profile, permission sets and permission set groups add object, field, user and app permissions, permission set licenses (PSLs) gate which permission sets a user's license can carry, and record visibility comes from org-wide defaults, role hierarchy and sharing (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=sf.standard_profiles.htm&type=5).

Service agent users get org-wide defaults Internal, the permission set group `AgentforceServiceAgentUserPsg` (bundling `Agentforce Service Agent User`, `Data Cloud User` and `Prompt Template User`), the permission set `Agentforce Service Agent Secure Base`, and an agent-specific `<Agent_Name>_Permissions` permission set that is edited to grant object access (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=ai.agent_user.htm&type=5).
Service agent users are assigned the `Agentforce Service Agent Secure Base` permission set (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=ai.agent_user.htm&type=5).

`sf org create agent-user` assigns the `Einstein Agent User` profile and the permission sets `AgentforceServiceAgentBase`, `AgentforceServiceAgentUser` and `EinsteinGPTPromptTemplateUser` (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_org_create_agent-user.html).

`AgentforceServiceAgentBase` is probably the API name of the Agentforce Service Agent Secure Base permission set (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/salesforce-cli-reference/guide/cli_reference_org_create_agent-user.html).

Any custom permission set for a service agent user must be compatible with the Einstein Agent license; permissions outside it fail with "The user license doesn't allow the permission" (for example, Edit Messaging Sessions) (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=ai.agent_user.htm&type=5).

Building service agents needs `Manage Agentforce Service Agents` and `Manage AI Agents`, or `Customize Application` (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=ai.agent_setup_explore_types.htm&type=5).
Building employee agents needs `Manage AI Agents` or `Customize Application` (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=ai.agent_setup_explore_types.htm&type=5).
Agentforce Studio and the new Agentforce Builder need `Manage AI Agents` (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=ai.agent_builder_studio.htm&type=5).

`Manage AI Agents` grants org-wide management of all agents, so Salesforce says to assign it narrowly (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=ai.agent_setup_explore_types.htm&type=5).

facts.fact: The `Agentforce Default Admin` permission set is referenced for the retiring Agentforce (Default) agent and Agent for Setup, alongside `View Setup and Configuration` (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=ai.agent_setup_enable_default.htm&type=5).
The Agentforce (Default) agent is retiring as of 2026-11-14 (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=ai.agent_setup_enable_default.htm&type=5).

Keep management and runtime permission sets apart: never put builder permission sets on the agent user or runtime permission sets on human admins (secondary) (https://www.salesforceben.com/agentforce-permissions-explained-agent-users-access-and-security/).

For least privilege, an external agent's runtime identity should be a Salesforce Integration user with `Minimum Access - API Only Integrations` with every permission removed from the profile itself, getting object and field access only through `Salesforce API Integration` PSL-backed permission sets (https://admin.salesforce.com/blog/2023/best-practices-for-configuring-your-integration-user).

Never use a System Administrator user as the execution user, because the token inherits that user's rights (https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2023/03/using-the-client-credentials-flow-for-easier-api-authentication).

facts.target: View all External Client Apps, view their settings, and edit their policies
facts.fact: Admins configuring ECA OAuth policies need the user permission View all External Client Apps, view their settings, and edit their policies (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_meta.pdf).

ECA pre-authorization uses `permittedUsersPolicyType = AdminApprovedPreAuthorized` with profiles (`commaSeparatedProfile`) or permission sets (`commaSeparatedPermissionSet`) (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=xcloud.preauth_user_app_access_through_eca.htm&type=5).

A Salesforce System Administrator (or a delegated admin with `Manage Users`, `Customize Application` or `Manage AI Agents`) creates the integration and agent users, assigns permission sets and PSLs, creates ECAs and enables Agentforce (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_setup_enable.htm&language=en_US&type=5).
A Data 360 admin assigns Data 360 permission sets (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=ai.agent_user.htm&type=5).

Licenses and Flex Credits are bought by the client's Salesforce account owner through the account executive (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_setup_enable.htm&language=en_US&type=5).

Standard Data 360 permission sets include `Data Cloud Admin`, `Data Cloud Architect`, `Data Cloud Data Aware Specialist`, `Data Cloud Marketing Manager` and `Data Cloud User` (assigned to service agent users); only `Data Cloud User` was confirmed in a current source (unverified) (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=ai.agent_user.htm&type=5).

With API Access Control on (Setup > API Access Control), API access is limited to allowlisted connected apps that are installed and unblocked, and installed apps default to Admin approved users are pre-authorized so only users whose profile or permission set is tied to the app can use it (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=xcloud.security_api_access_control_all_users.htm&type=5).
Some orgs must ask Salesforce Support to enable API Access Control (https://www.salesforceben.com/a-salesforce-admins-guide-to-auditing-connected-apps/ (secondary)).

The `Use Any API Client` permission bypasses API Access Control, but since the week of 2025-12-08 it no longer lets users self-authorize uninstalled connected apps (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005228838&language=en_US&type=1).

The ability to self-authorize uninstalled connected apps moved from `Use Any API Client` to the `Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps` permission (Summer '25), which Salesforce says to limit to trusted admins and developers (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.shr_use_any_api_restriction.htm&language=en_US&type=5).

Since September 2025 uninstalled connected apps are restricted to users with the new approval permission, so install-and-allowlist the agent's app before go-live or its users get blocked (https://admin.salesforce.com/blog/2025/get-ready-for-changes-to-connected-app-usage-restrictions).

Third-party tools such as DBAmp broke in orgs with API Access Control on (reported 2025-11-04) (secondary) (https://community.cdata.com/ideas/if-you-use-api-access-control-salesforce-change-may-stop-dbamp-on-nov-4-2025-1722).

facts.fact: There is a known article on Developer Console behavior when API Access Control is enabled; check it before enabling the control in orgs where developers use Dev Console (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005132451&language=en_US&type=1).

ECA OAuth policies include IP relaxation and session/refresh-token policies, with refresh-token expiry set under App Authorization > OAuth Policies, and profile login IP ranges and org trusted IP ranges also apply (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_meta.pdf).

Hyperforce lets customers choose the region their org runs in (examples: U.S., U.K., Germany, India, Japan, and more), and customer data is generally stored in the org's country when the services in use are available there, though some products have components elsewhere (https://www.salesforce.com/products/platform/hyperforce/).
Hyperforce has no extra cost (https://www.salesforce.com/products/platform/hyperforce/).

EU Operating Zone is a paid Hyperforce offering that stores and processes EU customer data within the EU boundary, with 24/7 EU-based support (https://www.salesforce.com/products/platform/hyperforce/).
EU Operating Zone stores and processes EU customer data within the EU boundary (https://www.salesforce.com/products/platform/hyperforce/).

Salesforce has zero data retention agreements with external LLM partners such as OpenAI and Azure OpenAI: prompts and responses are deleted after the response returns (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.generative_ai_trust_arch.htm&language=en_US&type=5).
Azure OpenAI is an external LLM partner under a Salesforce zero data retention agreement (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.generative_ai_trust_arch.htm&language=en_US&type=5).

Salesforce-managed models hosted inside the Salesforce trust boundary, for example Anthropic Claude, keep data inside that boundary under the same zero data retention policy (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/trust.html).

The Trust Layer masks detected PII with placeholders before prompts leave Salesforce and de-masks responses, but masking is disabled when an agent action calls a prompt template and still applies to prompt templates used directly (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_trust_data_masking.htm&language=en_US&type=5).

Other Einstein Trust Layer controls include dynamic grounding, toxicity detection, prompt defense and an audit trail with feedback stored in Data 360 (https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?language=en_US&id=sf.generative_ai_trust_layer.htm&type=5).

Salesforce Shield bundles Event Monitoring (80+ event types including agent actions, user and agent activity, streaming to SIEM), Platform Encryption (BYOK and externally held keys starting with AWS, covering Data 360 data), Field Audit Trail (up to 200 fields per object, up to 10 years) and Data Detect (https://www.salesforce.com/platform/shield/).
Event Monitoring is a Salesforce Shield component with 80+ event types including agent actions and streaming to SIEM (https://www.salesforce.com/platform/shield/).
Shield Platform Encryption supports BYOK and externally held keys starting with AWS, and covers Data 360 data (https://www.salesforce.com/platform/shield/).
Shield Field Audit Trail covers up to 200 fields per object for up to 10 years (https://www.salesforce.com/platform/shield/).
Data Detect is a Salesforce Shield component (https://www.salesforce.com/platform/shield/).
Shield components can be bought separately and pricing is quote-based (https://www.salesforce.com/platform/shield/).

Shield Event Monitoring tracks what data humans and AI agents access and is positioned for securing Agentforce deployments, while agent session tracing and the Trust Layer audit trail are stored in Data 360 (https://www.salesforce.com/platform/shield/).

Salesforce maintains compliance certifications and attestations; commonly cited names are SOC 1, SOC 2, SOC 3, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017 and 27018, PCI DSS, HIPAA-eligible and FedRAMP (Government Cloud), though the portal page did not list names (unverified) (https://compliance.salesforce.com/en).

Flex Credits list at USD $500 per 100,000 (EUR 500, GBP 400, JPY 60,000, AUD 700, SEK 5,000); a standard Agentforce action costs 20 Flex Credits (about $0.10) and an Agentforce Voice action costs 30, as shown on the pricing page on 2026-11-14 (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/pricing/).

The Flex Credit metering unit is the action (a specific function that an AI agent executes), and Flex Credits were introduced in May 2025 (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/pricing-update-2025/).
Flex Credit usage is tracked in near real time in Digital Wallet, which is free for customers with Digital Wallet-enabled products (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/pricing/).

Third-party guides say each action includes up to 10,000 tokens and that sandbox actions cost 16 credits, but neither is on the official pricing page (secondary) (https://www.jitendrazaa.com/blog/salesforce/salesforce-agentforce-credits-cost-model-complete-guide-2026/).

facts.fact: Agentforce per-conversation pricing is USD $2 per conversation (EUR 2, GBP 1.60), positioned for external customer-facing agents, and Help Agent Resolutions are listed at $2 (USD only), shown 2026-11-14 (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/pricing/).
Conversation pricing, Agentforce add-ons and Agentforce 1 Editions are not available on the PayGo or Pre-Commit Flex Credit models (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/pricing/).
Agentforce add-ons for Sales, Service, Field Service and Operations list at $125/user/month, shown 2026-11-14 (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/pricing/).
Agentforce Industries add-ons list at $150/user/month, shown 2026-11-14 (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/pricing/).

The `Agentforce User License` lists at $5/user/month, requires Flex Credits and deploys agents company-wide with access to limited CRM objects, shown 2026-11-14 (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/pricing/).
The `Agentforce Coworker User License` lists at $50/user/month including 30 MB of indexing per user per month, shown 2026-11-14 (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/pricing/).

The Agentforce add-ons went GA on 2025-06-17, replacing Einstein add-ons, and include unmetered Agentforce usage for licensed employees and Prompt Builder (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/pricing-update-2025/).
Agentforce 1 Editions went GA on 2025-06-17, replacing Einstein 1 Editions (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/pricing-update-2025/).
Announced 2026-09-03, Core includes 500,000 Flex Credits, Advanced 1 million and Max 2.75 million per org per year (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/salesforce-simplifies-editions-2026/).
Max Edition is listed from $550/user/month including the Agentforce add-on and includes 2.75 million Flex Credits per org per year (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/pricing/).
Advanced Edition includes 1 million Flex Credits per org per year (announced 2026-09-03) (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/salesforce-simplifies-editions-2026/).
The earlier Agentforce 1 Edition included 1 million Flex Credits and 2.5 million Data Services Credits per org per year (2025-06-17) (https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/pricing-update-2025/).

Salesforce Foundations is listed at $0, including Agentforce Builder, Prompt Builder, Agent Script, Agentforce Coworker and Agentforce Vibes, shown 2026-11-14 (https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/pricing/).

Data 360 uses Flex Credits at $500 per 100k (interchangeable between Data 360 and Agentforce), or Profiles at $240 per 1k profiles/year and Enterprise Profiles at $420 per 1k profiles/year; ingestion is free and Agentforce pricing examples exclude Data 360 credits, shown 2026-11-14 (https://www.salesforce.com/data/pricing/).
Legacy Data Services Credits remain for existing Data 360 customers (https://www.salesforce.com/data/pricing/).

Daily API request allocation (Limits Quick Reference, updated 2026-09-11): Enterprise Edition (and Professional with API access) gets 100,000 + (licenses x calls per license) + purchased API Call Add-Ons with 1,000 calls per `Salesforce` or `Salesforce Platform` license; Unlimited and Performance use 5,000 calls per license; Developer Edition gets 15,000; a Full sandbox gets 5,000,000 unless created from a template (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.pdf).

The API allocation is enforced on the org-wide aggregate over 24 hours, not per user; REST, SOAP, Bulk API, Bulk API 2.0 and most Connect REST APIs count, calls from installed managed packages count, and some Salesforce apps such as the Salesforce mobile app don't (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.pdf).

API usage shows in the `Sforce-Limit-Info` header, `/services/data/vXX.X/limits` and the API Request Limit per Month entitlement (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.pdf).

Paid active orgs get limited soft API overage up to a hard cap, while trial orgs, Developer Edition and sandboxes get none; past the cap calls fail with HTTP 403 `REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.pdf).
Extra API calls can be bought in increments of 200 to 10,000 per 24 hours (https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2024/11/api-limits-and-monitoring-your-api-usage).

Concurrent long-running requests (20 seconds or longer) are capped at 25 in production orgs and sandboxes and 5 in Developer Edition and trial orgs (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.pdf).
REST and SOAP calls time out after 10 minutes, and query calls follow SOQL limits (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/salesforce_app_limits_cheatsheet.pdf).
Shield is a paid add-on with quote-based pricing (https://www.salesforce.com/platform/shield/).
EU Operating Zone is a paid add-on with quote-based pricing, while Hyperforce itself has no added cost (https://www.salesforce.com/products/platform/hyperforce/).
